item.title: Guest opinion: Closing Churchill Avenue is no solution for preventing suicides
item.description: Teenage suicide is always a tragedy, and when it happens in our community, it looms larger, and darker, because one of “ours,” often for reasons unknown, has chosen to take their life on the train tracks. But one of the city’s proposed solutions, closing the the Churchill Avenue crossing, is deeply flawed and should be reconsidered. The post Guest opinion: Closing Churchill Avenue is no solution for preventing suicides appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.title: Palo Alto police arrest suspect in downtown sexual battery
item.description: Palo Alto police officers arrested a 33-year-old man from San Jose this week on suspicion of sexually assaulting an unhoused woman while she was sleeping downtown last month. The post Palo Alto police arrest suspect in downtown sexual battery appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.title: With awards and flamingos, Palo Alto hopes to boost disaster preparedness
item.description: Your best resource is your closest resource. That is a saying that Ken Dueker, director of Palo Alto’s Office of Emergency Services, is fond of sharing with members of the volunteer army that is quietly helping the city prepare for the next big disaster. item.title: Palo Alto’s iftar dinner offers space for reflection, celebration
item.description: If Uzma Minhas had to use one word to describe her third annual city-sponsored community iftar dinner, she would say “inspiring.” Close to 200 people shared a meal together in the Lucie Stern Community Center last Saturday to break the fast many practicing Muslims partake in during the month of Ramadan.
